audit_findings.title: The valuation date is after the iMerit rerun trigger, but the bridge remains pre-close
audit_findings.magnitude: $170.0 million upfront consideration plus up to $140.0 million of earnouts; $310.0 million combined equals $1.92 per diluted share and 6.54% of base equity value; acquired owner earnings unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: A closing would reduce cash or increase debt and contingent claims in the bridge while adding iMerit's owner earnings and growth to the operating valuation.
audit_findings.evidence: Our future cash requirements will depend on many factors, including our rate of revenue growth, our investments in strategic initiatives like acquisition of complementary businesses, capital expenditures and continued stock repurchases, including accelerated stock repurchases under our board-authorized stock repurchase program, which may require the use of significant cash resources and/or additional financing.
audit_findings.explanation: The supplied record demonstrates that the September 5 valuation passed its July 31 rerun trigger, but it does not establish whether or when the transaction closed. The known consideration is substantial, and the unknown acquired earnings could offset or exceed the financing and cash effects. The resulting perimeter mismatch is reasonably capable of changing the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the closing announcement or subsequent filing, actual closing date, cash paid, financing raised, contingent consideration recognized, post-close share count and iMerit owner earnings; rerun the operating value and bridge on the same post-close perimeter.

audit_findings.title: Historical owner earnings may understate the current floating-rate interest burden
audit_findings.magnitude: June 2026 gross debt of $381.250 million was $82.500 million above December 2025 gross debt of $298.750 million; first-half 2026 interest annualizes to $18.038 million, only $0.427 million or 0.18% above FY2025 interest and the $240.9 million anchor, respectively
audit_findings.mechanism: Because this is an equity-level owner-earnings DCF with principal not deducted, current interest expense must reduce projected owner earnings.
audit_findings.evidence: Our debt portfolio is on floating interest rates and is therefore fully exposed to interest rate fluctuations.
audit_findings.explanation: The possibility is valid, but the filed current-period interest burden does not demonstrate a material error. The annualized increase over FY2025 is less than one-fifth of one percent of anchor owner earnings and is far too small to close the $4.14-per-share gap between market price and the bull value. Additional acquisition financing is unresolved and is addressed through the iMerit perimeter rerun.
audit_findings.action: Normalize interest using current average debt, the applicable SOFR margins and commitment fees, and rerun if iMerit financing changes the debt balance or rate materially.

audit_findings.title: Capitalized client-transition costs may escape the reinvestment deduction
audit_findings.magnitude: Contract-fulfillment additions exceeded amortization by $11.349 million in 2024 and $3.201 million in 2025; first-half 2026 amortization exceeded additions by $0.602 million; other capitalized operating-cost additions are unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: If the OE calculation retains amortization expense but does not substitute the associated recurring cash additions, owner earnings and potentially the historical trend anchor are overstated.
audit_findings.evidence: Costs related to such transition activities are contract fulfillment costs, and thereby classified under “Other current assets” and “Other assets” in the consolidated balance sheets, and are recognized over the expected duration of the relationship with customers, under “Cost of revenues” in the consolidated statements of income.
audit_findings.explanation: The filings demonstrate material timing differences between fulfillment-cost cash additions and amortization, including a 2024 shortfall equal to 5.7% of that year's reported owner earnings. The effect was much smaller in 2025 and reversed in first-half 2026, so the record does not establish the sustainable annual adjustment. Contract-acquisition, customer-payment and cloud-implementation additions also have not been fully traced.
audit_findings.action: Reconstruct each OE year by adding back the relevant amortization and deducting actual cash additions for contract fulfillment, contract acquisition, customer payments and capitalized cloud implementation; then recompute the trend anchor and all scenarios.

audit_findings.title: Unaccrued Indian tax demands are a claim ahead of common equity
audit_findings.magnitude: $44.376 million net demand at June 30, 2026, equal to $0.27 per diluted share and 0.94% of base equity value; $7.436 million of payments or bank guarantees had been provided
audit_findings.mechanism: An adverse settlement would consume cash or require a direct deduction from the equity bridge; associated recurring tax effects could also reduce owner earnings.
audit_findings.evidence: The aggregate amount demanded by Indian tax authorities (net of advance payments) as of December 31, 2025 and 2024 is $ 42,205 and $ 49,588 , respectively.
audit_findings.explanation: The claim is demonstrated, while an adverse outcome is not. Even charging the entire June net demand against equity would reduce value by only about $0.27 per share, versus the $4.14 gap between the market price and bull value, so the filed amount cannot change the current no-buy conclusion. Unfiled interest and penalties remain unquantified.
audit_findings.action: Update the proceedings and separate cash deposits from guarantees; rerun the bridge if the estimated loss, including filed interest and penalties, grows materially beyond the disclosed net demand.

audit_findings.title: A pension prior-service obligation was recorded outside net income
audit_findings.magnitude: $21.210 million unfunded status at December 31, 2025 plus $1.177 million of additional 2026 prior-service cost; June 2026 noncurrent retirement-benefit liabilities were $41.507 million, equal to $0.26 per diluted share and 0.88% of base equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: The unfunded benefit claim belongs ahead of common equity unless its required catch-up contributions are deducted from projected owner earnings.
audit_findings.evidence: These legislative changes have resulted in an increase in the projected benefit obligation and the same has been recognized as prior service cost in OCI.
audit_findings.explanation: The OCI treatment and unfunded obligation are demonstrated. Even using the broader June retirement-benefit liability as a full bridge deduction would reduce value by only about $0.26 per share, far below the $4.14 market-price gap to bull value. Normal service and amortization costs are already entering reported earnings.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the June 2026 funded-status reconciliation and contribution schedule; deduct any unfunded amount not already represented through projected contributions, and rerun only if the updated obligation increases substantially.

audit_findings.title: The cash bridge may treat foreign cash as fully distributable
audit_findings.magnitude: $249.3 million of the $283.8 million June 2026 cash and short-term investments was foreign; complete exclusion would equal $1.54 per diluted share and 5.26% of base equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: Withholding taxes, legal reserves or trapped-cash restrictions reduce the surplus cash that can be added to the equity bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: As of December 31, 2025 and 2024, we had $328.4 million and $340.6 million, respectively, in cash, cash equivalents and short-term investments, of which $285.8 million and $296.0 million, respectively, is located in foreign jurisdictions that upon distribution may be subject to withholding and other taxes.
audit_findings.explanation: Foreign concentration is demonstrated, but the actual incremental tax or restriction is unquantified. Even the extreme assumption that all $249.3 million of foreign cash is unavailable would reduce value by $1.54 per share, still leaving the market price above the $30.95 adjusted bull value. It therefore cannot reverse the current no-buy conclusion, although it can lower reported intrinsic value.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile June cash by jurisdiction, exclude restricted and customer funds, calculate incremental withholding or repatriation taxes, and replace the face-value bridge addition with the distributable after-tax amount.
